text:
oncall-bot: PAGE: severity=high · Canary release-2026-03-17-psi failing · metric=error_rate(canary)>5% · ticket=https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1324 · impacted=3 customers :fire_engine:

maria: I'm on it, taking incident lead. tagging @sre oncall and @eng-runtime. Can someone confirm automated rollback status?

leo: checking automated rollback controller.. looks like the controller saw the spike but did NOT fire. lots of 502s in canary, threshold was 4% but our window config was 60s; we had a 45s spike — race condition.

jamal: ugh. so controller missed it due to window. I can flip manual kill-switch and run manual rollback now. Who will own verification?

maria: jamal please execute manual rollback and flip the FF to disable the new routing. alex, you help with verification (smoke + customer checks)? olivia, prep initial customer-impact note.

jamal: running commands now

jamal: ```
# flip feature flag kill-switch
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/release-routing/disable

# start manual rollback
redwood rollout rollback --id release-2026-03-17-psi --mode=manual --reason="canary 502 spike" --force
```

jamal: kill-switch API returned 200 ok :white_check_mark:

sre-ops-bot: Rollback job queued: job_id=rj-20260317-09-43; started by jamal; estimated time=90s

alex: watching logs and health checks. Running canary-smoke and live traffic probes.

alex: canary-smoke output:
```
[ok] /health 200
[fail] /generate 502 x 12
```

leo: stack traces show nginx upstream aborted with ECONNRESET from inference runtime. correlating with recent kernel param tweak (tcp_fin_timeout) from earlier deploy.

maria: note that automated rollback config needs immediate follow-up. create a follow-up ticket after incident.

olivia: initial customer-impact: 3 paying customers had degraded requests routed to canary, ~2% of total RTs, errors ~40% for affected users. Drafting message for status page now. ETA 15m for public update.

product-ops: do we need to page SEs for those 3 customers? Recommend yes if they are on enterprise plans.

maria: yes please page customer success for the three listed in the ticket. alex confirm if error rates drop post-rollback before we page them.

sre-ops-bot: Rollback progress: 25% -> 50% -> 75%

jamal: rollback completed, job_id=rj-20260317-09-43, result=success :white_check_mark:

alex: re-running canary-smoke

alex: canary-smoke now:
```
[ok] /health 200
[ok] /generate 200 latency=120ms
```

leo: logs look clean, nginx upstream errors stopped. metrics pipeline shows error_rate(canary)=0.4% over last 2m.

olivia: published status page update: "We detected a regression in a canary rollout affecting a subset of customers. A manual rollback was performed and service has recovered. We are investigating root cause and will follow up." link=https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INF-1324

maria: good. verification checklist:
- confirm canary error rate <1% for 10m
- confirm customer retries successful for affected customers
- revert the kernel param change in staging and reproduce locally
- create follow-up: fix controller window calculus + add guard for transient spikes

jamal: I've opened INF-1325 with steps to harden automated rollback window + add canary backoff. assigned to leo.

leo: ack. i'll reproduce and push a patch to controller. also adding a safety net to ignore windows <30s.

product-ops: customers paged and acknowledged receipt. CS will coordinate 1:1 if needed.

maria: incident status -> mitigated. leaving thread open for postmortem notes. assigning follow-ups: INF-1325 (rollback controller fix), INF-1326 (post-deploy kernel param checklist), INF-1327 (audit flag toggles)

alex: quick note — we should add a synthetic that hits /generate under canary load to catch short spikes.

maria: agreed. add to postmortem. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
